title: Making Your Opinion Clear
text:
Many writers use opinion language to show their stance. Expressions such as 'I believe', 'in my view' and 'it seems to me' signal that a statement is personal rather than a proven fact. Readers who notice these phrases can judge how strongly the writer feels. For example, 'I am convinced' expresses much more certainty than 'I suppose'.

Stance can also be shown through adverbs and adjectives. A writer who says the plan is 'clearly flawed' is more forceful than one who calls it 'perhaps a little weak'. However, careful writers often add hedges such as 'arguably' or 'to some extent' to avoid sounding absolute. Such choices show that the writer is open to other points of view.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does 'I am convinced' express?
options: The same level of doubt as 'I believe'
A fact that needs no opinion

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what is the purpose of adding hedges such as 'arguably'?
What can be inferred about a writer who uses many hedges?
options: They always write in a formal style
They are certain about everything they write
They may be willing to consider other opinions

questions.text: Why might a reader pay attention to phrases like 'in my view'?
options: Because they make the sentence grammatically correct
Because they are required in every academic text
Because they prove the writer is an expert
Because they show the statement is personal, not a proven fact

vocabulary.definition: a position or opinion a writer takes on a topic
words that make a statement less certain or less absolute
strong and convincing in how it is expressed
complete, with no exceptions or doubt

paragraph_translations: Muitos escritores usam linguagem de opinião para mostrar sua posição. Expressões como 'I believe', 'in my view' e 'it seems to me' indicam que a afirmação é pessoal, e não um fato comprovado. Leitores que percebem essas frases podem avaliar o quanto o autor se sente seguro. Por exemplo, 'I am convinced' expressa muito mais certeza do que 'I suppose'.

A posição também pode ser mostrada por meio de advérbios e adjetivos. Um autor que diz que o plano é 'clearly flawed' é mais contundente do que quem o chama de 'perhaps a little weak'. No entanto, escritores cuidadosos costumam acrescentar atenuadores como 'arguably' ou 'to some extent' para não soarem absolutos. Essas escolhas mostram que o autor está aberto a outros pontos de vista.
